title: Family
description: Learn how to talk about your family members, siblings, and relatives in Japanese.
guidebook:
### Talking About Family in Japanese

In Japanese, the words you use for family members often depend on whose family you are discussing!

When talking about your own family to others, use humble terms: **chichi** (father), **haha** (mother), **ani** (older brother), and **ane** (older sister). This shows politeness by lowering your own circle.

When talking about someone else's family or calling out to your own relatives directly, polite forms are used instead, like **otousan** (father) and **okaasan** (mother).

Additionally, Japanese specifies age among siblings: **ani** and **ane** for older siblings, and **otouto** (younger brother) and **imouto** (younger sister) for younger ones.

phrases.native: My older brother is in Tokyo.

phrases.romanization: Watashi ni wa imouto ga imasu.

phrases.target: 赤ちゃんが笑っています。

phrases.native: There are four people in my family.

phrases.romanization: Otouto wa se ga takai desu.

phrases.target: 祖母はお茶が好きです。
phrases.romanization: Sobo wa ocha ga suki desu.
